text:
nina: Heads up — CI started failing on the nightly SAST job after the RBAC tidy yesterday. error from scanner: `KMS: permission denied (decrypt)` so the analyzer can't load secrets to run some tests.
maggie: ugh. which SA is affected?
nina: `projects/redwood-prod/serviceAccounts/scanner-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` appears to be missing `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` after the role cleanup.
zack: i saw a spike in triage alerts this morning too, might be related. can someone paste the exact error trace?
nina: pasted from CI: ```Error: failed to decrypt secret: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = requestor does not have permission to perform action 'cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt' on resource projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/app-secrets```
infra-bot: automated note: RBAC change applied by @mike at 2024-09-18T02:14Z — removed broad role `roles/owner` from infra-service-accounts.
maggie: ok that explains it. quick fix: re-grant the least-privileged role to that SA scoped to the specific key, not project-wide.
security-oncall: tagging for triage. we also need to confirm audit logging for KMS calls — I can't find a matching log entry for the failed decrypt in Cloud Audit Logs for that SA window.
zack: i queried logs briefly: `gcloud logging read "protoPayload.methodName=\"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt\" AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=\"scanner-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com\"" --limit 5 --project=redwood-prod` and got nothing.
maggie: hmm — either the call never reached KMS because it was blocked by IAM earlier, or audit logs aren't being routed/retained for that key.
nina: CI shows the call attempted, got permission denied. should produce an audit entry. maybe log sink filters?
security-oncall: action items: 1) infra to temporarily grant `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` on key resource to SA (owner: @maggie) 2) infra to confirm KMS audit logs are enabled/retention + add sink if missing (owner: @zack) 3) security to update runbook for scanner SA privileges and PR template to lock key-binding scoping (owner: @nina) 4) open incident ticket for the CI break so product teams are aware.
maggie: i'll open a PR with the scoped binding: ```resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding" "scanner_decrypt" {  crypto_key_id = "projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/app-secrets"  role          = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"  members       = ["serviceAccount:scanner-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]}``` will add tests for least privilege.
zack: i'll check the logs pipeline. if audit logs were accidentally excluded by sink filter, we can backfill by enabling the sink and running `gcloud logging read` for the time window to pull any retained entries. if no entries exist, we need to assume the API call was rejected pre-KMS and rely on CI traces.
infra-bot: temp grant created by @maggie at 2024-09-18T03:20Z (expiry 1h) — scoped to the key.
nina: CI rerun succeeded after the temp grant :party_parrot: — can we make the temp grant expire only after PR merges?
maggie: i'll update the PR to include a GC policy for a service account binding and request review from @security-oncall and @cloud-infra.
security-oncall: please also add a short note in the incident ticket about missing audit evidence and the plan to harden sinks/retention — compliance will ask.
zack: timeline — i'll finish audit pipeline check in 45m and post logs snippet. if we need an audit backfill script, i'll propose one.
nina: thanks all. assigning owners in the ticket: infra (zack) logs + retention, infra (maggie) RBAC PR, security (nina) runbook + incident note. i'll follow up in #release-war-room if anything blocks ship.
security-oncall: one more: consider using KMS CMEK per-environment keys + key access approvals for prod — reduces blast radius. add as follow-up RFC after this stabilizes.
nina: agreed. documenting next steps in the ticket. thanks! :thumbsup:
